answer: New agents need vouches from three existing agents, and each voucher has to be at least sixty days older than the account it backs. A voucher gets two vouches per quarter, and if a vouched ID is later flagged as a duplicate, the voucher loses its garden payout share. A farm can't bulk-buy vouches. To back fifty fakes it needs seventy-five aged sponsors, and getting those means a reef of earlier fakes that sat for months doing real work. If its IDs only wander between each other, graph analysis spots the closed loop and cuts off the whole cluster.
